The paper reviews over 150 innovative articles on passive structural RCS reduction published over 24 years.
RCS is measured in square meters (m²) and represents the effective area of a target as seen by radar.
Active RCSR is most suitable for low frequencies but suffers from high fabrication complexity, cost, and narrow bandwidth.
The Salisbury screen, proposed in the 1950s, was one of the first RAM structures but had high thickness and operated only at normal incidence.
AMC/EBG checkerboard structures have achieved monostatic RCSR bandwidths ranging from 54% to over 113%.
Modi et al achieved 91% bandwidth without requiring the traditional 180° ±37° reflection phase difference criterion.
Zheng et al's three-cell composite AMC structure achieved 95% bandwidth, surpassing earlier two-cell designs.
Aperiodic AMC/FSS arrangements provide 13% more bandwidth than periodic arrangements at normal incidence.
Ameri et al designed a structure with 90% monostatic RCSR bandwidth that remained stable for both TE and TM polarization up to 50° and 30° oblique incident angles respectively.
Zaker and Sadeghzadeh achieved one of the widest bandwidths (113.33%) using a double-layer chessboard-like configuration.
High impedance surfaces (HIS) were first proposed by Sievenpiper et al in 1999 and consist of resistive film and dielectric substrate.
Metamaterial absorbers (MA) and perfect metamaterial absorbers (PMA) transform electromagnetic energy into heat and typically operate near resonance frequency.
Polarization rotation reflective surfaces (PRRS) reflect incoming waves with 90° polarization rotation using a single type of unit cell.
The paper covers RCS reduction techniques for un-planar structures including cylindrical, curved, and cubic geometries.
Conventional absorbing materials produce heat that makes targets detectable by infrared detectors, a significant operational limitation.
Frequency selective surfaces (FSS) can be designed with periodic or aperiodic arrangements for different performance characteristics.
The reflection coefficient phase of AMC/EBG structures varies from +180° to -180° with increasing frequency.
At resonance, the reflection coefficient magnitude and phase of an EBG/AMC structure are approximately +1 and 0° respectively.
A perfect electric conductor (PEC) surface reflects waves with a phase of 180°, which is used as a reference for comparison.
Double-layer FSS structures with aperiodic arrangements achieved 50% monostatic 10-dB RCSR bandwidth compared to 36% for periodic arrangements.
Randomized arrangement structures of AMC cells perform better for bistatic RCS reduction compared with periodic arrangements.
The paper emphasizes that most conventional techniques have been performed only for monostatic RCSR at normal incident angles, ignoring wave polarization.
Modern passive cancelation techniques focus on achieving wideband, wide-angle, and polarization-independent RCS reduction.
The structural RCS of a target depends on physical shape, frequency, orientation, polarization properties, and constitutive materials.
Antenna RCS is a significant contributor to overall target RCS and depends on subcomponents such as antennas and sensors.
